questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I always make sure to like and comment __by my friends’ posts__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**on my friends’ posts**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct preposition to use with "like and comment" in the context of social media is "**on**".
 
• We say "like and comment **on** a post" to indicate the action is performed regarding that post.
 
• **Options 1, 2,** and **4** do not fit standard English usage in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"I always make sure to like and comment **on my friends’ posts**__."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "of my friends’ posts"** is incorrect because "comment of" is not standard usage.
 
• **Option 2: "in my friends’ posts"** is incorrect, as "comment in" is not typically used for social media posts.
 
• **Option 4: "around my friends’ posts"** is incorrect; it does not convey the intended meaning.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

A) The beauty pageant has / B) been postponed farther due to / C) limited representation coming / D) from other states.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary error lies in part B of the sentence, where the word "**farther**" is incorrectly used.
 
• The word "**farther**" is typically used to indicate physical distance, whereas "**further**" is used for abstract or metaphorical contexts.
 
• Since the delay is not related to physical distance, the correct word here should be "**further**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part B** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The beauty pageant has been postponed further due to limited representation coming from other states."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "The beauty pageant has" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **C: "limited representation coming"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **D: "from other states."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Fungi are tiny organisms found everywhere—in nature, in our homes and even in and on _______ bodies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**our**'. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• The blank in the sentence refers to "bodies" that include humans collectively. Hence, the possessive pronoun **"our"** is appropriate. 
 
• Options **1 ("their")**, **3 ("your")**, and **4 ("my")** do not fit the context because the sentence is talking about humans in general. 
 
• **Option 2 ("our")** correctly indicates collective ownership of the bodies being referred to. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Fungi are tiny organisms found everywhere—in nature, in our homes and even in and on **our**__ bodies."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 1 ("their"):** Incorrect because "their" implies ownership by another group, which does not match the context of the sentence. 
 
• **Option 3 ("your"):** Incorrect because "your" refers to the person being spoken to, which does not fit the general statement. 
 
• **Option 4 ("my"):** Incorrect because "my" refers to the speaker's own body, which limits the general scope of the sentence.

questions.question:

They _________ a problem with the internet connection, but it’s fixed now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**had**'. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• The verb "**had**" is the simple past tense form of the verb "**have**." 
 
• The sentence states that there was a problem in the past that has now been resolved, so the past tense "**had**" is appropriate. 
 
• **Options 2, 3**, and 4 are grammatically incorrect and do not fit the context of the sentence. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"They **had**__ a problem with the internet connection, but it’s fixed now."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 2: "make"** is incorrect because "make" does not fit the context of the sentence describing a past issue. 
 
• **Option 3: "do"** is incorrect as it is not used to describe having a problem. 
 
• **Option 4: "have"** is incorrect because the sentence refers to a completed action in the past, requiring the past tense "had."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Never judge a book by its cover

options.text: You should always judge people based on their possessions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Never judge a book by its cover"** means that appearances can be deceptive and one should not evaluate someone or something based solely on external looks. (कभी भी किसी को उसके बाहरी रूप से मत आंकें)

 
 
• **Example:** Though the house looked shabby from the outside, it was beautifully furnished and luxurious inside.
 
 
 
• **"Appearances can be deceiving"** implies that external looks do not always reflect the true nature or value of something. (दिखावा हमेशा सच नहीं होता)
 
 
• **Example:** She seemed unfriendly at first, but she turned out to be one of the kindest people I have ever met.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom emphasizes not judging or making assumptions based on superficial appearances.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Beautiful things are always valuable** (सुंदर चीजें हमेशा मूल्यवान होती हैं): This statement is incorrect as beauty does not necessarily equate to value.

 
 
• **Example:** The painting was beautiful, but it had no real historical or monetary value.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: First impressions are always accurate** (पहला प्रभाव हमेशा सही होता है): This is false as first impressions often fail to reveal the true nature of someone or something.
 
 
• **Example:** At first, I thought he was unfriendly, but later I realized he was just shy.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: You should always judge people based on their possessions** (आपको हमेशा लोगों को उनकी संपत्ति के आधार पर आंकना चाहिए): This is incorrect as possessions do not define a person’s character or worth.
 
 
• **Example:** Though he had few belongings, his generosity and kindness showed his true nature.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**which**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage refers to "Plastic products, (1)__________ are often designed for single use," which requires a relative pronoun that connects "plastic products" to the describing clause.
 
• "Which" is the correct relative pronoun to introduce a non-defining relative clause providing extra information about "Plastic products."
 
• Other options like "when," "where," and "whose" do not fit grammatically or contextually in the sentence.
 
• Therefore, "which" fits well and maintains the grammatical structure and clarity of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The widespread use of plastic has become a significant environmental concern due to its impact on ecosystems and human health. Plastic products, (1). which__ are often designed for single use, contribute to massive amounts of waste that persist in landfills and oceans (2)__________ hundreds of years. This persistent waste not only clogs waterways and harms marine life but also breaks down into microplastics that enter the food chain, posing risks to (3)__________ wildlife and humans. The (4)__________ of plastic is overshadowed by its long-term environmental costs, making it imperative to explore sustainable alternatives and reduce plastic consumption. Addressing plastic usage requires (5)__________ collective effort to adopt more eco-friendly practices, support recycling initiatives and invest in innovative materials that minimize environmental impact.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When: Used to refer to time, does not fit the context of describing "plastic products."
 
• Where: Used for places/locations, not suitable here.
 
• Whose: Used to indicate possession, which is not required in this sentence.
 
• Which: Correctly introduces additional information about "plastic products."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**for**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank is part of the phrase "persist in landfills and oceans (2)__________ hundreds of years," which requires a preposition indicating duration.
 
• "For" is the correct preposition to express the length of time (hundreds of years) that plastic waste remains in the environment.
 
• Other options like "among," "since," and "across" do not fit grammatically or contextually in this sentence.
 
• "For" clearly indicates the duration that the waste persists, making it the most appropriate choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The widespread use of plastic has become a significant environmental concern due to its impact on ecosystems and human health. Plastic products, (1). which__ are often designed for single use, contribute to massive amounts of waste that persist in landfills and oceans (2). __for__ hundreds of years. This persistent waste not only clogs waterways and harms marine life but also breaks down into microplastics that enter the food chain, posing risks to (3)__________ wildlife and humans. The (4)__________ of plastic is overshadowed by its long-term environmental costs, making it imperative to explore sustainable alternatives and reduce plastic consumption. Addressing plastic usage requires (5)__________ collective effort to adopt more eco-friendly practices, support recycling initiatives and invest in innovative materials that minimize environmental impact.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Among: Used for being included or surrounded by, not suitable for expressing time duration.
 
• Since: Refers to a starting point in time, not a duration.
 
• For: Correct preposition to indicate a period of time ("for hundreds of years").
 
• Across: Used to indicate movement from one side to another, not time duration.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.

__

• "Both" is the correct choice as it is used to refer to two entities together—here, wildlife and humans.
 
• Other options like "yet," "but," and "because" do not fit grammatically or contextually in this sentence.
 
• "Both wildlife and humans" clearly indicates that risks apply to the two mentioned groups.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The widespread use of plastic has become a significant environmental concern due to its impact on ecosystems and human health. Plastic products, (1). which__ are often designed for single use, contribute to massive amounts of waste that persist in landfills and oceans (2). __for__ hundreds of years. This persistent waste not only clogs waterways and harms marine life but also breaks down into microplastics that enter the food chain, posing risks to (3). __both__ wildlife and humans. The (4)__________ of plastic is overshadowed by its long-term environmental costs, making it imperative to explore sustainable alternatives and reduce plastic consumption. Addressing plastic usage requires (5)__________ collective effort to adopt more eco-friendly practices, support recycling initiatives and invest in innovative materials that minimize environmental impact.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Yet: Means "however," not suitable for connecting two nouns.
 
• But: Used for contrast, not to connect two subjects equally affected.
 
• Because: Used to show reason, not suitable here.
 
• Both: Correctly joins two entities (wildlife and humans) equally impacted by the risks.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**a**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank is part of the phrase "requires (5)__________ collective effort to adopt more eco-friendly practices..."
 
• "Collective effort" is a singular, countable noun phrase, so it requires the indefinite article "a" before it.
 
• "An" is used before words with a vowel sound, but "collective" starts with a consonant sound.
 
• "The" is used for something specific or previously mentioned, but here it refers to any collective effort in general.
 
• No article is not correct, as the phrase needs an article before the singular countable noun "effort."

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The widespread use of plastic has become a significant environmental concern due to its impact on ecosystems and human health. Plastic products, (1). which__ are often designed for single use, contribute to massive amounts of waste that persist in landfills and oceans (2). __for__ hundreds of years. This persistent waste not only clogs waterways and harms marine life but also breaks down into microplastics that enter the food chain, posing risks to (3). __both__ wildlife and humans. The (4). __convenience__ of plastic is overshadowed by its long-term environmental costs, making it imperative to explore sustainable alternatives and reduce plastic consumption. Addressing plastic usage requires (5). __a__ collective effort to adopt more eco-friendly practices, support recycling initiatives and invest in innovative materials that minimize environmental impact.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• A: Correct indefinite article for "collective effort."
 
• An: Used before vowel sounds, not suitable here.
 
• The: Refers to specific things, not general collective effort.
 
• No article: Not grammatically correct with singular countable noun "effort."
